chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh narrated from his father, from Abī al-Bakhtarī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever misses the salat of the ʿEid should pray four rakʿahs.

The proper understanding of this narration is option, because one who prays alone has the choice between praying two rakʿahs according to the arrangement of the salat of the two ʿEids, and between praying four however he wishes, although the superior form is the two rakʿahs according to the arrangement of the salat of the ʿEid.

key_terms.التَّخْيِيرُ: the presence of a legal choice between two valid options
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: the more meritorious or superior option
key_terms.تَرْتِيبِ صَلَاةِ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the prescribed arrangement of the salat of the two ʿEids
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of salat performed in the ʿEid format

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they miss the salat of ʿEid according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling for one who misses the salat of ʿEid. It indicates that such a person may pray four rakʿahs, while the juristic explanation given here clarifies that a person praying alone has a choice between two rakʿahs in the form of the ʿEid salat and four rakʿahs, with the two-rakʿah form being superior.
